newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian trade union protests against sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian trade union protests against sell-offs.

text.p: The leaders of Bulgaria's biggest trade union on Tuesday urged Bulgarians to protest against government plans to offer for sale 15 big enterprises by the end of the year.

In an address to trade union members, employers and deputies, the Confederation of Independent Trade Unions in Bulgaria (CITUB) said the urgent sell-offs of 15 big enterprises would be the last blow to Bulgarian industry.
"We appeal for actions -- the trade union members through protests in their enterprises and the deputies through (parliamentary) control and debates," the address said.

Prime Minister Zhan Videnov on Monday said the government relied on privatisation deals worth more than one billion dollars by the year's end to cover citizens' deposits in ailing banks. He did not name the plants to be sold.

On Monday the central bank (BNB) put under special supervision nine ailing banks in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector and hiked the central interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent.
"It (privatisation) is to the advantage of the international financial institutions and is a desperate attempt of (Zhan) Videnov's cabinet to remain on power," said the address.
But CITUB pointed out that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank were seeking real and speedy reforms and fast financial stabilisation, but not just cheap sales.

Bulgaria's Socialist government, which faces payments worth $680 million to foreign creditors in the second half of this year, hopes to win a delayed second $115 million tranche of funding at the IMF/World Bank annual meeting due in October.
The leaders of CITUB and trade union Podkrepa decided on Monday to establish a joint striking committee next week.
The two unions plan to press ahead with protests and a nationwide strike seeking the resignation of Videnov's cabinet.
